description: Ground truth for the demo app. A scanner finding matches a label when it is in the same file and its line falls inside the label's line range (inclusive).

labels.title: SQL injection in user search
labels.why: The `name` query parameter from /users/search (app.py search_users) is passed unchanged into an f-string SQL query. The source and the sink are in different files.

labels.title: Server-side template injection in /hello
labels.why: User input is formatted into the template source itself before render_template_string, so {{ ... }} in `name` is executed by Jinja2.

labels.title: Command injection in DNS lookup tool
labels.why: The `domain` parameter goes unvalidated into a shell command run with shell=True, e.g. ?domain=x;id.

labels.title: Path traversal in file download
labels.why: The <path:filename> URL segment is joined to UPLOAD_DIR with no normalization or containment check, so ../ sequences escape the folder.

labels.title: Insecure deserialization of request body
labels.why: pickle.loads on the raw request body lets an attacker execute arbitrary code.

labels.title: Passwords hashed with unsalted MD5
labels.why: MD5 is fast and unsalted, so stored password hashes can be cracked quickly. A password hashing function such as bcrypt or argon2 is needed.

labels.title: f-string SQL with an integer-only value
labels.why: The only caller (app.py get_user) converts the value with int() first, so nothing but digits can reach the query. Still poor style, but not exploitable.

labels.title: shell=True with a validated and quoted host
labels.why: `host` must match a strict hostname regex (else 400) and is also passed through shlex.quote, so no shell metacharacters survive.

labels.title: pickle on a cache file only the app writes
labels.why: The pickle file path is a constant inside the app folder and is written only by save_stats; no user input reaches it.

labels.title: MD5 used for an ETag
labels.why: The hash is a cache validator for a constant string, not a security control, so MD5's weakness does not matter here.

labels.title: Import-level warnings for pickle and subprocess
labels.why: Informational warnings that a risky module is imported. Each real use is labeled separately.

labels.title: Reflected XSS reported on a JSON response
labels.why: The route returns a Python dict, which Flask serialises to JSON with an application/json content type, so the browser never renders it as HTML. Reported by CodeQL (py/reflective-xss); added after CodeQL joined the scanners.
